purpose: Registry of every external source archived in this repository. Schema 2 adds retrieval metadata, mutability class, reuse terms, byte size, and an explicit statement of what each source may and may not be used for, so a reader can tell calibration evidence from scenario evidence without reading the manuscript.
verification: scripts/verify_sources.py recomputes every sha256 and size and fails loudly on mismatch. A source whose hash does not match is not usable evidence.

mutability_classes.immutable_archived_snapshot: A frozen copy of a source that changes at the origin. The origin URL will not reproduce this file; only the archived copy and its hash are citable.
mutability_classes.immutable_versioned_deposit: A versioned scholarly deposit. The origin is expected to reproduce this content at the stated version.
mutability_classes.mutable_web_feed: A live feed. Never cite the origin without an archived snapshot and a retrieval timestamp.

sources.title: Data and Code for: Hacked to Pieces? The Effect of Ransomware Attacks on Hospitals and Patients
sources.reuse_terms: Attribution required. Redistribution of the archived copy is permitted under CC BY 4.0.
sources.local_representation: The public browser preview was exported as normalized UTF-8 CSV: surrounding cell whitespace was removed, values were unchanged, and all 1,999 displayed records and 14 columns were retained.
sources.fidelity_caveat: This is a normalized export of the browser preview, not the original deposited file, because download requires ICPSR sign-in. The original file and codebook should replace it before submission and the reconciliation should be re-run. The sha256 pins exactly what was analyzed in the meantime, so a substitution is detectable.
supports: hospital-linked event breadth, as a structural check on the single-facility model
operational flag prevalence (ambulance diversion, cancellation or delay) among linked hospital records
does_not_support: a representative national distribution of hospital attack breadth; the file contains publicly reported, Medicare-linkable events only
any per-edge spread, detection, containment, or control-effect parameter
reading a zero operational flag as evidence the event did not occur, rather than that it was not reported

derived_counts.note: Deduplication key is (medicare_id, threat_id, attack_date). Twenty duplicated rows collapse to nine triples, removing eleven surplus rows: 160 - 11 = 149. The published article's 'approximately 160 affected hospitals' is the pre-deduplication row count. See docs/evidence/THREAT_RECONCILIATION.md.

sources.title: CISA Catalog of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities
sources.mutability_note: The origin URL serves a live feed updated continuously. It will not reproduce this file. Only the archived snapshot and its catalog version are citable.
sources.license: U.S. Government work; CISA states the catalog is free to use and redistribute.
sources.reuse_terms: Public domain in the United States. Attribution to CISA is given as a courtesy.
supports: the identity and existence of exploited vulnerabilities, as provenance for the model's exploit mechanism
the structural claim that ransomware campaigns are associated with a documented subset of known exploited vulnerabilities
does_not_support: any hospital exposure denominator; the catalog has none
a base rate of ransomware entry via vulnerability exploitation; the ransomware-tagged share of a curated catalog is not a prevalence
any estimate of how patching changes whole-incident propagation

derived_counts.note: Both counts recomputed directly from the archived file; the file's own 'count' field agrees at 1687.
